2 Bends
It is therefore necessary to plan and prepare in order to negotiate a bend successfully:
 On the approach and before entering the bend:
- Adapt the speed of your vehicle, changing, if necessary to a lower gear that is appropriate for the bend.
- If it necessary to brake do so before entering the curve, never when negotiating the bend.
- Place the vehicle, as close as possible to the right hand side of the roadway.
(Página 223 del manual 'Learning to drive')

Safe driving
 
2 Bends
Whilst driving around the bend / inside the curve:
- Turn the steering wheel softly, without crossing the hands, and ensuring that the steering is proportionate to the degree and angle of the bend.
- Avoid coarse or hurried movements of the steering wheel. Don’ accelerate harshly or fiercely and avoid hurried or abrupt braking. If necessary for any reason, to brake whilst in the curve you should to so softly, thus trying to avoid the potential to skid.
- Accelerate softly and progressively from the start of the curve to help the tyre grip and adhere to the road surface. This action helps the vehicle recover its course and maintain traction.
(Página 223 del manual 'Learning to drive')

The last important moment occurs days or weeks after the accident (late mortality).

For combinations of vehicle-trailer or semi-trailer up to 750 kilograms MAM, the driver must carry the ITV card of the towing vehicle, where will be confirmed that the vehicle is equipped with a towbar that is compatible with the trailer as well as the ITV card of the light trailer itself.
(Página 25 del manual 'Learning to drive')

3 Documentation for the vehicle  
 
3.2 Card relating to the technical inspection of the vehicle (ITV card)
The technical inspection card records the following:
On the front, certification of the vehicle’s characteristics.
On the reverse side, the record of regular inspections.
Certain modifications carried out after the registration of the vehicle must be carried out with the corresponding permit and must be stipulated on the ITV card.
(Página 25 del manual 'Learning to drive')

4.2.4 Inflation pressure
If the inflation pressure is greater than that recommended:
There is a reduction of the surface area in contact with the road surface and therefore reduced adhesion.
The wear is more pronounced through the centre of the tread.
The irregularities of the ground are not absorbed, thus producing vehicle vibrations.
The suspension elements undergo greater deterioration.

5 Generic speed    
 
5.3 Minimum generic speed
When you drive below these minimum limits you are said to travel at an abnormally reduced speed. This is considered an inadequate speed, as there is an increased risk of danger and a higher risk of a collision as a result of people overtaking the slower moving vehicles. It also adds to road congestion as it hampers the movement of other road users.
(Página 174 del manual 'Learning to drive')
